h.select_rule: Keep hypotheses you rate at least 55% likely true but expect other models to rate below 50%, and name the specific naive reasoning that would mislead them. Drop anything you rate below 50% yourself, and anything obvious from structure alone. Keep fields and directions diverse.
h.strategy: Propose a broad, varied set of conditional hypotheses covering many different edited fields, conditioning fields and both directions. For each, briefly note your own probability that it holds and how an intuitive reader would judge it.

hyps.why: Adding a conv on the direct input-output edge where none existed gives a large gain.
Turning a removed edge into a 3x3 conv gains more than replacing an existing op.
Replacing none with a conv restores a path into the output, a larger gain than swapping one op for another.
Removing a good conv hurts more than removing a weak op.
Dropping a 3x3 conv into the output is a large loss versus dropping a pool.
Deleting a 3x3 conv on the first edge is more harmful than deleting a weak op.
Redundant with a strong conv on a parallel path into the output, so diminishing returns.
The direct 3x3 conv already supplies features, so the extra conv is less valuable.
Without the direct edge, the conv on edge 4 matters more for output features.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with a pool loses learnable capacity, a worse change than replacing other ops.
